content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion periods (e.g., after 70+ price days), especially when sentiment is mixed; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending strongly.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67…), model tends to misalign with true volatility; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.
